description: OpenViveksha node type registry. Each node type defines config fields (JSON Schema), ports, and execution semantics. Port types: TXT, PROMPT, TOOLS, ANY. Fields marked "secret": true are write-only (reads omit them; values may reference ${ENV_NAME}, resolved at run start). EMBED, AUDIO, HARMONICS, SECURITY, FILES are reserved for future versions.

portTypes.PROMPT: Normative prompt object: { system: string, messages: [{ role: "user" | "assistant" | "tool", content: string, toolCalls?, toolCallId? }], tools?: [{ name, description, inputSchema }] }. Produced by role/tools, consumed by tools/llm; provider-llm maps it 1:1 to /chat/completions.
portTypes.TOOLS: Tool definitions from an MCP server (array of { name, description, inputSchema }).

nodeTypes.label: Input Channel
nodeTypes.summary: External trigger via webhook (HTTP POST with secret). Emits { message } on trigger.

secret.description: Required header X-Ingress-Secret on webhook POST. Compared constant-time. May be ${ENV_NAME}.

webhookUrl.description: Assigned by runtime when active. The HTTP server binds 127.0.0.1 unless explicitly told otherwise.

execute.outputs: When triggered: { message } (seed, laws §5). When a value arrives on `reply`, the channel may forward/deliver it (v0.1: the run result is the delivery).

nodeTypes.label: Role
nodeTypes.summary: Composes the system prompt (SOUL) for this agent from the incoming message. Produces a PROMPT for llm/tools.

execute.outputs: { prompt: { system: soulPrompt, messages: [{ role: "user", content: message }] } }. On the `reply` input: passes the reply through (loop back-edge delivery).

nodeTypes.label: LLM Provider
nodeTypes.summary: Calls an OpenAI-compatible or Ollama chat endpoint with the composed PROMPT. Returns { reply }.

maxTokens.description: Guideline: >= 8192 when the graph uses tool calls — smaller values truncate JSON tool arguments.

execute.outputs: { reply } — final text, or a { tool_calls: [...] } envelope when the model requests tools (consumed by the tools node).

nodeTypes.label: Tool Loop
nodeTypes.summary: Agentic tool loop: takes PROMPT + TOOLS, runs LLM <-> tool-call iterations until a final text reply or maxIterations.

inputs.name: reply
inputs.description: LLM reply passed through the loop (back-edge).

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: Prompt augmented with tool schemas (and later tool results).

execute.outputs: Without tools input: passthrough prompt, reply passthrough. With tools: executes the tool loop (may invoke MCP tools), final { reply }. Termination: a reply without tool_calls ends the loop.

nodeTypes.label: MCP Source
nodeTypes.summary: Connects to an MCP server (stdio or streamable HTTP) and emits its tool definitions on `tools`.

command.description: stdio: executable command line. WARNING: arbitrary code execution — a canvas is code.

authToken.description: Optional bearer token sent as Authorization header (http). May be ${ENV_NAME}.

execute.outputs: { tools: [ { name, description, inputSchema } ] } from the connected MCP server; { tools: [] } when inactive/unreachable — never blocks the graph (laws §8).

nodeTypes.label: Conversation History
nodeTypes.summary: Memory passthrough: injects prior conversation turns into the prompt and records new turns. Storage key: (canvasId, nodeId, sessionId) — two history nodes keep separate memories.

depth.description: How many recent turns to inject. 0 = unlimited.

execute.outputs: On `prompt`: appends stored turns before the current user turn and records the user turn. On `reply`: records the assistant turn BEFORE emitting (so a direct llm.reply → chat.reply wire can never outrun the record), passes the reply through. Turn shape: { role: "user" | "assistant", content: string }; storage: SQLite, survives restarts.

nodeTypes.label: Chat / Output
nodeTypes.summary: Conversation entry/output node. Typically the run start (seeded with { message }) and the sink whose `reply` input terminates the run (laws §10).

execute.outputs: As start node: seeded by the executor, never re-executes (laws §5/§10). Otherwise: forwards the incoming reply as its message output.
